correctness.rationale: For every \(a\ge3\), \(\varepsilon\in\{0,1\}\), and \((a,\varepsilon)=(2,1)\), the eight listed endpoint families have independently identifiable two-occurrence longest borders. The one-character extension lemma proves that every available neighboring context is mismatched. The intervals all cross cut \(a+2\), are distinct, and count \(a+5=\lfloor n/2\rfloor+1\). Parity covers every \(n\ge13\). Executed border-counting checks cover 57 parameter instances, 1211 intervals, and 15 complete cut enumerations; symbolic reasoning handles all parameters.

value.rationale: A recent primary paper leaves the sharp local cut-density constant open and exhibits \(\lfloor(n-1)/2\rfloor\) binary crossing MCSs at each length. A single finite strict-half example cannot show persistence, while the all-length family proves a strict excess over half for every \(n\ge13\). This is a structural persistence boundary rather than a merely tabulated numerical improvement. The gain over the published witness is additive and the leading asymptotic constant remains \(1/2\); these material limitations are stated.
